app.name: RoxPlan
app.tagline: Periodized HYROX training that adapts to you, and won't let you overreach.

note.twoDayWeek: Two sessions a week will build real race readiness. If you can find a third, it's the single biggest step up for a first race — but this plan works as it is.

zone.zone2: Zone 2 — steady aerobic base, you could hold a conversation
zone.threshold: Threshold — goal race pace, comfortably hard

readiness.notEnoughTime: There isn't enough time to build race fitness safely before this date. Trying to would raise your injury risk without meaningfully improving your finish.
readiness.whatThisPlanIs: So this plan does something different: it gets you familiar with all eight stations, teaches you what running off a station feels like, and gets you to the start line fresh and knowing what to expect.
readiness.pacingGuidance: Start slower than feels right. The first run is the easiest one you'll do, and going out hard is the most common way a first race unravels.
readiness.raceDayLogistics: Know the station order, bring your own kit for the farmers carry grip, and walk the venue before you start if you can.
readiness.stationTechnique: Station technique — all eight, light load
readiness.singleCompromisedRun: One compromised run — a station, then run
readiness.noSimulations: No race simulations. A full simulation this close would cost you more in recovery than it gains you in readiness.
readiness.noNewMaximalLoading: No new maximal loading. This isn't the window to find out what your heaviest sled feels like.
readiness.noVolumeIncrease: No increase over your current training volume. Holding steady is the goal.
readiness.considerLaterRace: It's worth asking whether a later race would serve you better. There's no prize for racing this one under-prepared, and a date 12 weeks out would let you arrive genuinely ready.
readiness.considerRelayOrDoubles: If you'd rather race this date, Relay or Doubles splits the work between you and a partner or team — much less total load, and the same event-day experience.
